description:
A guard comparing against a list, tuple or map literal is refused; Elixir allows it:

    def empty?(t) when t == [], do: true
    def empty?(_t), do: false
    def main(), do: dbg([empty?([]), empty?([1])])

fz (interp and run): "compiler2 entry guards for `empty?/1` are not dispatch-pure and cannot be planned". Elixir prints [true, false].

Works: `t == 0`, `t == :a`, `t == "s"`. Fails: `t == []`, `t == [1]`, `t == {}`, `t == %{}`, `[] == t`, `t === []`. Not needed by the distiller.
title: A guard compares against a list, tuple or map literal, as in Elixir
